# Requirements Quality Checklist: P-RF09 — Settings Dashboard

**Purpose**: Risk-weighted requirements-quality review of spec.md, covering the three functional areas (dashboard chart/narrative, account deletion/LGPD, profile+biometric+logout) plus cross-cutting consistency, with extra depth on the two highest-risk areas: account deletion (irreversible, legally sensitive per RNF05) and dashboard aggregation (the most conditional/edge-case-heavy logic).
**Created**: 2026-10-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Account Deletion & Data Lifecycle (LGPD / RNF05)

- [ ] CHK001 Is "every piece of data tied to it" (RNF05) enumerated as a concrete, exhaustive list of locally-held data categories (session, cached profile, entries, chat, other), rather than left to an open-ended "any other locally held user data" phrase? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019, §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK002 Does the spec specify whether vault/PIN and biometric-preference local storage are included in or excluded from the account-deletion data wipe, given they are a separate on-device concern from the account itself? [Gap, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the requirement for a second concurrent delete attempt (FR-022) scoped to "Apagar tudo" specifically, and does the spec confirm no other in-flight request (e.g., a profile save) is expected to block or race with an account-deletion request? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the spec define the dialog's behavior if the session expires while the delete-confirmation dialog is already open and the user has not yet tapped "Apagar tudo" vs. after tapping it but before the response resolves? [Edge Case, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK005 Are the specific failure modes for `DELETE /account` (timeout, no connection, malformed response, expired session) each traceable to a distinct, non-overlapping user-facing outcome, or could two of them produce indistinguishable error text? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK006 Is "malformed response" for the delete call defined precisely enough (e.g., any non-success body) to be distinguished from "no response" so the retry-ability of each is unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK007 Does SC-004 ("zero account deletions occur without explicit confirmation") have a corresponding requirement covering accidental dismissal (tap-outside, back-gesture, OS back button) as equivalent to "Cancelar", not merely the two button taps? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-021, §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the irreversibility claim ("no way to undo it afterward") paired with a requirement stating there is no grace period, soft-delete, or recovery window on the backend side that the spec needs to account for? [Assumption, Spec User Story 2]

## Dashboard Aggregation & Narrative

- [ ] CHK009 Is the "roughly-equal time slices" bucketing rule (Assumptions) precise enough to be independently reproduced — i.e., does it specify how a non-evenly-divisible date range's remainder days are distributed among the ten bars? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK010 Does the spec define expected behavior when the account's full date range is shorter than ten days (e.g., 3 days of history across >1 entries), beyond "naturally produces a chart with some empty bars"? [Edge Case, Spec Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the boundary between the "exactly one entry" state (FR-004) and the "two or more entries" state (FR-005) specified in terms of the aggregate's entry count rather than UI appearance, so it cannot be misread as applying to bucket count instead? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK012 Are all distinct dashboard states (empty, single-entry, multi-entry/narrative-pending, multi-entry/narrative-shown, narrative-unavailable, aggregate-error) individually named/identifiable so no two can be confused with each other in an implementation? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003–FR-007]
- [ ] CHK013 Does the spec address what the chart area shows while the aggregate request is still in flight (a loading state), or is this left undefined between "nothing yet" and the first of the enumerated states? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK014 Is retry behavior specified for the aggregate-error state (FR-007 says "with a way to retry") — e.g., does retrying re-request both the aggregate and, if it succeeds, the narrative, or only the aggregate? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK015 Does the spec distinguish, for narrative failures, between a narrative that fails outright and one that times out, or are both intentionally treated identically under "narrativa indisponível" with no behavioral difference? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the requirement that the dashboard "MUST be recomputed from a fresh backend call every time Settings is opened" (FR-008) explicit about whether "opened" includes returning to Settings via back-navigation from a sub-screen, or only a fresh app-level navigation to it? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008]

## Profile, Biometric Toggle & Sign-Out

- [ ] CHK017 Is there a requirement guarding against a second concurrent name-save or biometric-toggle request analogous to FR-022's guard on "Sair"/"Apagar tudo", or is this double-submission case intentionally left uncovered for lower-risk actions? [Gap, Consistency, Spec §FR-022]
- [ ] CHK018 Is the display name's valid character set specified beyond a length bound (1–80 characters) — e.g., are whitespace-only names, emoji, or leading/trailing whitespace addressed? [Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK019 Does the spec define how the initials avatar is derived from a display name that has only one word, non-Latin characters, or is empty/default, so the avatar's content is unambiguous for every name state the spec allows? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK020 Is "the app's authentication entry point" (used identically by FR-016 and FR-019) defined with enough precision in the spec itself, or does it depend entirely on an external assumption resolved outside this spec's own requirements? [Traceability, Spec Assumptions, §FR-016, §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK021 Does the spec specify what the biometric toggle displays while its own save request is in flight (already-toggled optimistically vs. a pending/disabled state), distinct from the final success or revert-on-failure states in FR-013/FR-014? [Gap, Coverage]

## Cross-Cutting Consistency & Traceability

- [ ] CHK022 Are the generic failure phrases "timeout, no connection, malformed response" used across FR-007/FR-012/FR-014/FR-020 intended to cover every one of the backend's documented error codes (including rate-limiting), or could a code outside that phrase's literal scope produce an undefined outcome? [Completeness, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007, §FR-012, §FR-014, §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK023 Is the relationship between this spec's generic "existing expired-session handling... takes over exactly as it does elsewhere" (Edge Cases) and each individual FR's own failure-handling language made explicit, so a reader can tell session-expiry is an exception to FR-level retry/error requirements rather than a case those FRs also separately need to handle? [Consistency, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK024 Do FR-016 (sign-out) and FR-019 (account deletion) each unambiguously state which locally held data categories they clear, such that their difference (entries/chat cache cleared only on deletion) is a requirement a reader can derive from the spec text alone, not just inferred from the two being adjacent? [Clarity, Consistency, Spec §FR-016, §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK025 Are success criteria SC-001 through SC-006 each traceable to at least one specific functional requirement and acceptance scenario, with no measurable outcome left floating without a corresponding testable FR? [Traceability]
